draft.title: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
card: The United Nations (UN) was formed in 1945, after the Second World War. Its members wanted to prevent such suffering happening again.
In 1948 the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. It set out rights that belong to every person, in every country.
Australia's H. V. Evatt was President of the General Assembly in 1948. He led the assembly that passed the Declaration.
The Declaration is a statement of shared ideals. It is not a treaty, so it does not by itself make a country change its laws.
draft.remember: The 1948 Declaration set out rights for all people, and Australia's Evatt led the assembly that passed it.

a.q: Why did the UN adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948?
opts: To set out rights for every person after the war's suffering
To give each member country a legal duty to pass new laws
To list the rights of only the countries that won the war
To end the Second World War by setting terms of peace
a.why: The Declaration came after the horrors of the Second World War and set out rights for every person. It was not a treaty that forced laws on countries, and the war had already ended.
a.clue: Think about what the world had just lived through, and who the rights were for.

b.q: Tom says the Declaration made Australia change its laws in 1948 because Evatt led the General Assembly. What is wrong with his claim?
opts: It was a statement of ideals, not a treaty forcing new laws
Evatt led the assembly only after it had passed the Declaration
It set out rights only for people living in Australia
It was adopted by Australia alone, not by the United Nations
b.why: The Declaration was a shared statement of ideals and did not by itself make any country change its laws. Evatt's role was leading the General Assembly that passed it, but that does not turn it into a law for Australia.
b.clue: Check what kind of document the Declaration is.
